徳.meaning: Riding up a ski <part>chairlift</part>, a kind old man hands his <part>ten</part> spare mittens to shivering kids, then lowers a <part>net</part> of oranges to the people queuing below. His <part>heart</part> is the warmest thing on the mountain. Everyone talks about his <kanji>benevolence</kanji>.
徳.on: Even the lift's clock slows its tick-<sound>tock</sound> so he can finish.

慈.meaning: A knight's dragon foe falls and tears its wing. Instead of finishing it, she opens her <part>sewing kit</part>, threads a needle and stitches the wing back, her <part>heart</part> thumping. The dragon flaps off, blinking, saved by <kanji>mercy</kanji>.
慈.on: Next week the dragon pulls her muddy <sound>jee</sound>p out of a ditch to say thanks.
慈.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' squeaks a mouse in her saddlebag, sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and she lets it nibble her <sound>coo</sound>kie: to cherish.

捜.meaning: A sailor drags an <part>anchor</part> along the seabed while holding a <part>lantern holder</part> over the side, its beam sweeping every rock. She dropped her lucky ring overboard. All night the light swings left and right in a full <kanji>search</kanji>.
捜.on: At dawn she finds the ring stuck in a sunken bar of <sound>so</sound>ap.
捜.kun: A <sound>sa</sound>rdine swims up to help, smelling strongly of <sound>ga</sound>rlic.

隙.meaning: A climber plants her <part>pennant</part> on a cliff and spots a <part>little</part> crack beside it, just wide enough for one finger. Peering in, she sees the <part>sun</part> shining from the other side. The whole mountain is split by one thin <kanji>crevice</kanji>.
隙.on: A <sound>gec</sound>ko squeezes out of it and licks her finger.
隙.kun: She posts a roll of <sound>su</sound>shi and a <sound>ki</sound>wi through the gap for it.

呪.meaning: A <part>big brother</part> reads magic words from a comic to scare his sister, but now his <part>mouth</part> won't behave: every word comes out as a frog. Croak, croak. His sister finds the cure on the next page, grins, and keeps him under the <kanji>spell</kanji> a little longer.
呪.on: A <sound>ju</sound>ry of frogs on the sofa croaks him guilty.
呪.kun: '<sound>No</sound>t my <sound>ro</sound>cket!' he croaks, as a frog hops into his toy spaceship.

俵.meaning: A farmer hangs a fat straw sack of rice on a <part>coat hook</part> by the door. Its <part>surface</part> is woven so tight that not one grain slips out, though the hook groans. Rice farmers trust only one thing with a harvest: a straw <kanji>bag</kanji>.
俵.on: His neighbour, a lady in high <sound>hee</sound>ls, sits on it doing slow <sound>yo</sound>-yo tricks.
俵.kun: The hook snaps, the sack lands on his <sound>ta</sound>co, and he wails '<sound>Wah</sound>!' into his <sound>ra</sound>men.

胴.meaning: A tailor measures the <part>moon</part> for a suit and finds its waist is the <part>same</part> size as its chest and hips: no curves at all, just one round barrel middle. He gives up on the belt and sews a plain tube for its <kanji>trunk</kanji>.
胴.on: He stuffs the tube with bread <sound>dough</sound> to test the fit.

囚.meaning: A zookeeper counts the lions at closing time, steps into the wrong <part>cage</part>, and click. Now the lions stroll free outside while one <part>person</part> stands behind the bars, his keys lying on the grass out of reach. The zookeeper has been <kanji>captured</kanji>.
囚.on: He tries to hook the keys with the toe of one long <sound>shoe</sound>.
囚.kun: A lion on <sound>to</sound>p of the cage kindly drops him a bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men.

衡.meaning: At a busy <part>crossroads</part>, a street performer balances a wriggling <part>fish</part> on the tip of her nose while traffic whizzes past all four ways. Cars honk, the fish flaps, and she doesn't wobble an inch. Perfect <kanji>equilibrium</kanji>.
衡.on: For the finale she adds an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne on the fish's tail.

棟.meaning: A builder chops the tallest <part>tree</part> in the forest and lays it along the very top of a new house, pointing <part>east</part> so the first light of dawn runs down it. Every rafter leans on it like ribs on a spine. It's the <kanji>ridgepole</kanji>.
棟.on: He walks along it on tiptoe, one big <sound>toe</sound> at a time.
棟.kun: At sunrise a <sound>moo</sound>se balances up there, tangled in a <sound>ne</sound>t of fairy lights.

庶.meaning: In a market <part>shed</part>, anyone can walk in and cook: a farmer, a sweeper, a baker's boy. They pass round one battered <part>tray</part> and roast sweet potatoes over the <part>hot coals</part> on the floor. No crowns, no butlers: it's the hall of the <kanji>commoner</kanji>.
庶.on: They sell the leftovers through the hatch of a tiny <sound>sho</sound>p next door.

唇.meaning: At the beach a man finds an empty <part>clam</part> shell, paints its two halves bright red and holds it in front of his <part>mouth</part> as a party mask. Every time he talks, the shell flaps open and shut. Everyone admires his giant <kanji>lips</kanji>.
唇.on: A crab nips his <sound>shin</sound>, wanting its neighbour's shell back.
唇.kun: A <sound>coo</sound>k slips <sound>chee</sound>se between the red shells, a <sound>bee</sound> steals it, and a kanga<sound>roo</sound> claps.

郎.meaning: A proud father waves a <part>pennant</part> at every school match, though his boy only sits on the bench. 'He's <part>good</part>! He's very good!' The boy finally scores, by accident, with his ear. Dad faints with joy: that's my <kanji>son</kanji>.
郎.on: Mum throws the boy a red <sound>ro</sound>se from the stands.
郎.kun: Years later the boy is a tall grown man. When he scores a real goal, an <sound>o</sound>tter cheers from the <sound>to</sound>p row and he leaps into the arms of the <sound>ko</sound>ala mascot.

絹.meaning: A spider sits in the <part>mouth</part> of a cave and spins <part>thread</part> all night by the light of the <part>moon</part>. By dawn she has woven a scarf so soft and shiny that the moon itself asks to borrow it. Only one cloth feels like that: <kanji>silk</kanji>.
絹.on: A dog drags the scarf into its <sound>ken</sound>nel as a fancy blanket.
絹.kun: She hides her second scarf in a <sound>ki</sound>wi crate in a <sound>noo</sound>k of the cave.

帆.meaning: A castaway has nothing special on his raft, just a <part>commonplace</part> beach <part>towel</part>. He ties it to an oar, holds it up to the wind, and whoosh, the raft skims across the bay into the harbour. The plainest towel makes a fine <kanji>sail</kanji>.
帆.on: In the harbour he swaps it for a pot of <sound>hon</sound>ey.
帆.kun: On the way he dangled a <sound>ho</sound>tdog from the oar for the gulls.

畜.meaning: Instead of a fence, a farmer ties each animal to a long string wound on a giant <part>spool</part>. At dinnertime she gives a gentle tug, and cows, goats, pigs and one sulky goose all trot home from the <part>rice field</part>. She's the only farmer who reels in her <kanji>livestock</kanji>.
畜.on: Every evening she feeds each of them one fat <sound>chick</sound>pea, which they fight over.

墜.meaning: A <part>regiment</part> of paper planes takes off in tight rows from the schoolyard. A gust hits, and one by one they spin, wobble and nose-dive into the <part>soil</part> of the flowerbed. The teacher counts the wrecks sticking out of the mud: a mass <kanji>crash</kanji>.
墜.on: A boy plucks them out of the mud with a pair of <sound>twee</sound>zers.
墜.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps the teacher, short and sharp, as the last plane drops.

譜.meaning: A composer can't sing, so she draws her <part>speech</part> instead: every word she says becomes a dot on five lines. Her marks are <part>universal</part>: a drummer in one country and a harpist in another play it exactly the same. Her chatter has become a <kanji>score</kanji>.
譜.on: The orchestra practises it lying on one huge rolled-out <sound>fu</sound>ton.

憶.meaning: An old sailor's <part>heartbeat</part> skips when he smells salt and tar, and an <part>idea</part> lights up like a bulb: the ship, the storm, the parrot he once had. Forty years vanish in one sniff. A smell is the fastest door to a <kanji>recollection</kanji>.
憶.on: Best of all, he remembers the <sound>oc</sound>topus that stole his hat.

机.meaning: A woodpecker opens an office. She taps a little <part>table</part> right into the side of a <part>tree</part>, adds a drawer for pencils and a hole for an inkpot, and sits behind it every morning in a tiny tie. Even birds need a <kanji>desk</kanji>.
机.on: She locks the drawer with a tiny brass <sound>key</sound>.
机.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' she sneezes, scattering <sound>coo</sound>kie crumbs over an <sound>e</sound>gg in the drawer.

穀.meaning: A <part>gentleman</part> spreads a picnic <part>blanket</part> beside a field of <part>grain</part>, and a <part>maiden</part> curtseys and joins him. Instead of cake, they shake the ripe heads into bowls and pour on milk: the world's first breakfast of <kanji>cereals</kanji>.
穀.on: A <sound>cock</sound>atoo swoops down and steals a beakful.

棋.meaning: A carver cuts a <part>tree</part> into tiny wooden figures and lines them up on a <part>bookshelf</part>. At night they climb down, march onto the board and argue over who gets the corner squares. Every one of them is a <kanji>chess piece</kanji>.
棋.on: Now the carver locks the shelf at night with a brass <sound>key</sound>.
棋.kun: The pieces still play another board game too, wearing <sound>go</sound>ggles to see the tiny lines: the game of go.

泌.meaning: A sponge cake soaked in syrup is <part>certain</part> it can hold more. The baker keeps pouring, and slow <part>water drops</part> squeeze out of every side, pooling on the plate. The cake sighs and keeps on dripping. Syrup always finds a way to <kanji>ooze</kanji>.
泌.on: A lady steps in the puddle and her high <sound>hee</sound>l sticks fast.

尿.meaning: A puppy at the castle trots up to the <part>flag</part> pole, sniffs it, lifts a leg, and a little stream of <part>water</part> splashes the base. The guards pretend not to see. That pole has been marked with dog <kanji>urine</kanji>.
尿.on: A guard down on one <sound>knee</sound> mops it up, while the puppy chases his slow <sound>yo</sound>-yo.
尿.kun: Then the puppy naps under a <sound>eu</sound>calyptus by the <sound>ba</sound>rbecue, on a heap of <sound>ree</sound>ds.

眉.meaning: A tiny sea captain plants a <part>flag</part> on a <part>pole</part> just above a giant's <part>eye</part>, claiming the hairy ridge as new land. The giant frowns, the ridge scrunches up, and the flag topples. The captain had landed on an <kanji>eyebrow</kanji>.
眉.on: A shiny <sound>bee</sound>tle lives in it and refuses to move out.
眉.kun: The giant's <sound>ma</sound>ma combs it flat with a <sound>eu</sound>calyptus twig.

諾.meaning: A <part>young</part> knight asks an old dragon if he may cross its bridge. The dragon thinks for a whole minute, then lets out one short word of <part>speech</part>: 'Fine.' The knight nearly falls over. He came with a sword and left with the dragon's <kanji>consent</kanji>.
諾.on: A <sound>duck</sound> waddles across behind him, nodding yes as well.

渦.meaning: A <part>cuckoo clock</part> falls into a pond and keeps ticking underwater. As its hands spin, the <part>water drops</part> follow, faster and faster, until the whole pond swirls round the clock like soup round a spoon. The cuckoo pops out, dizzy, in the middle of a <kanji>whirlpool</kanji>.
渦.on: A <sound>ca</sound>rp spins round and round with it, grinning.
渦.kun: A bowl of <sound>u</sound>don whirls past, topped with a slice of yu<sound>zu</sound>.

銘.meaning: A champion's <part>gold</part> trophy is too shiny for a sticker, so the jeweller takes a tiny chisel and cuts her <part>name</part> into its side, letter by letter, so deep that a thousand polishings won't rub it away. Those words in the metal are an <kanji>inscription</kanji>.
銘.on: Tiny swirls round the letters make a <sound>ma</sound>ze an ant could get lost in.

幽.meaning: A hermit moves into a <part>mountain</part> where two paths <part>twist</part> in and in, round and round, until no visitor can follow. Postmen give up; even echoes get lost. Alone with a goat, he has found the perfect place to <kanji>seclude</kanji> himself.
幽.on: His only visitor is a <sound>u</sound>nicorn who knows the way.
幽.kun: His pond is so deep that the <sound>fu</sound>ll moon sinks into it, and a <sound>ca</sound>rp nibbles its edge.

芋.meaning: A gardener sticks a <part>hat stand</part> in her vegetable patch as a scarecrow, and the crows just perch on it. But under the <part>grass</part> at its foot, something swells until it lifts the stand off the ground. She digs, and out comes a hairy brown root as big as a football: a giant <kanji>taro</kanji>.
芋.on: She slices it into a steaming bowl of hot <sound>u</sound>don.
芋.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' squeaks a mouse in the hole, waving a tiny <sound>mo</sound>p.
